question: When does physics advance in lockstep mode?
tldr: Once every motor has heard from its master, before the next read.
answer: Frames take no time and are answered at once. When every motor on every bus has had a frame, the cycle is done: if it ended with a write, physics advances now; if with a read, it advances just before the next read, so writes sent in between act during the step.
why: The 'owed' flag makes the order subtle: a read-ended cycle defers its step. Drawing it shows why a read-then-write master sees its writes' effect on the next read.
rate: every frame or packet the masters send; physics advances 1/hz per cycle

nodes.label: lockstep
nodes.explain: Computes how many timesteps make one period; the period must be a whole number of them.

nodes.label: wait_any
nodes.explain: No timeout: time stands still while no master sends.

nodes.label: run owed step
nodes.tldr: Before a read, run the deferred cycle
nodes.explain: If this frame reads and the last cycle ended with a read, physics advances one period now, so the read sees what the writes in between did.

nodes.label: deliver
nodes.tldr: Motors answer at once, current state
nodes.explain: CAN frames, Dynamixel packets or EtherCAT frames go to the dock as in real time, with no bus time.

nodes.label: Drydock::cycle_done
nodes.tldr: Has every motor been heard since last?
nodes.explain: Each bus keeps a 'heard' flag per motor, set on delivery; a master that leaves a motor out stalls time.

nodes.label: write ends cycle: step now
nodes.explain: A cycle ended by a write runs physics at once.

nodes.label: owed
nodes.tldr: A read-ended cycle not yet stepped
nodes.explain: Set when a read completes a cycle; cleared when its physics runs before the next read.

nodes.label: killed
nodes.explain: Ends on Ctrl-C or a socket error.
